verdicts.why: E = Pt = 1100 x 600 = 6.6 x 10^5 J, key B. 1.1 x 10^5 J (t = 100 s) and 6.6 x 10^4 J are decimal slips. Easy, one step.
3 and 6 in parallel give 2 ohm, plus 4 gives 6 ohm, key C. 9 ohm is the plain sum, 2 ohm the parallel only. Medium is generous, fine.
X/12 = 25/75 so X = 4 ohm, key A; 36 ohm is the inverted ratio. Null at 25 cm from the left with X on the left is stated clearly.
I = 2/(3.5+0.5) = 0.5 A, V = IR = 1.75 V, key D. 2.00 V (the emf) and 1.50 V are traps.
v_d = I/(neA) = 4/(5e28 x 1.6e-19 x 2e-6) = 2.5e-4 m/s, key C. 1.25e-4 is the area-halved slip, 2.5e-2 the exponent slip. Two-step, medium.
Sensitivity rises with a smaller potential gradient and a longer wire, so I and II, key B. III and IV do the opposite. Options are unique; NCERT 3.16.
Metal resistivity rises, intrinsic semiconductor resistivity falls with temperature: I and II, key A. Unique. NCERT 3.8.
Manganin has a near-zero temperature coefficient, which is exactly why it is used for standard coils: A and R true, R explains A, key A. NCERT 3.7.
Net emf 6 V, total resistance 3 ohm, I = 2 A, P = I^2R = 12 W, key B; 6 W and 24 W are plausible slips. Three simple steps: the label hard is too high, medium is right.
verdicts.repair: difficulty_label hard -> medium. Solver-visible text unchanged.
